page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.0 GHz. It features 3 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 10.67 GB per core. The hardware profile includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU (0.5 GPU count) providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1705.53 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 26.06 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory performance are generally weak. The multi-core stress-ng score is 5059.76, and the PassMark CPU score is 5574.75. Large block memory write bandwidth is average at 26.33 GB/sec, but read bandwidth is weak at 35.06 GB/sec. For LLM workloads, the server achieves average inference speeds on small 135M models (549.08 tokens/sec prompt processing, 125.03 tokens/sec text generation) but performs poorly on medium 7B models.

This server represents an entry-level GPU-accelerated option, offering a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring hardware acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core provides ample space for memory-resident datasets, though the overall compute and memory bandwidth limitations present a tradeoff. It is best suited for light GPU-accelerated tasks, small-scale LLM inference, basic machine learning prototyping, and applications that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon cores and NVMe storage.
